status_summary: SEC action so far is mostly proposals. In May 2026 the SEC proposed registered offering reform (91 FR 31022, published 2026-05-26: broader Form S-3 shelf eligibility and, through a definition of qualified purchaser, preemption of state registration for all registered offerings, not only exchange-listed ones), optional semiannual reporting, and simplified filer categories with wider scaled disclosure; a law-firm alert dated 2026-09-01 reports that all comment periods had closed and that final rules were expected soon, with no adoption reported; Federal Register listings of SEC final rules published from 2026-06-01 through 2026-10-17 show only technical and administrative rules. On 2026-09-30 the SEC requested comment on possible new routes to accredited investor status (a FINRA-developed exam and certain professional credentials), without proposing rule text for them. On the Consolidated Audit Trail it exempted certain personal-data reporting (2025-02-10), approved an amendment to cut its costs (2026-03-27) and issued a concept release on its future (2026-04-16, Release No. 34-105251), which seeks comment before any rulemaking and proposes no termination; the CAT remains in operation. Changes to Regulation A, Regulation CF, micro-offerings, finders and Rule 144 were not found in the sources reviewed.

timeline.event: SEC grants an exemption from the requirement to report certain personally identifiable information to the Consolidated Audit Trail.
SEC approves an amendment to the CAT NMS Plan to further reduce the costs of the Consolidated Audit Trail.

SEC seeks public comment on the Consolidated Audit Trail and other audit trails and data sources (concept release, Release No. 34-105251, docket S7-2026-12; Federal Register 2026-04-20); it seeks input before any rulemaking and proposes no termination.
SEC proposes amendments to permit optional semiannual reporting by public companies.

SEC proposes registered offering reform, including broader Form S-3 shelf access and preemption of state registration for all registered offerings (91 FR 31022, document 2026-10373, File No. S7-2026-17, published 2026-05-26; comments closed 2026-07-27).
SEC proposal published to enhance emerging growth company accommodations and consolidate filer statuses into two categories (comments closed 2026-07-20).

SEC press release 2026-96 seeks public comment on whether to designate additional routes to accredited investor status (passing a FINRA-developed exam, or holding a CPA license, CFA charter, CFP certification, or FINRA Series 79, 86 or 87 licenses); these are requests for comment, not proposed amendments, issued alongside proposals on adviser performance fees and closed-end funds.

title: Reduce SEC barriers to capital formation and terminate the Consolidated Audit Trail
uncertainties: The registered offering proposal (91 FR 31022) was read in review on 2026-10-17 through about 100,000 of 115,000 characters on federalregister.gov, covering its summary and main proposals; the semiannual reporting and filer-status proposals were read only as titles and summaries. The Federal Register lists of SEC proposed and final rules since 2025-01-20 (first 40 each) showed no Regulation A, Regulation CF, accredited investor, micro-offering, finder or Rule 144 rulemaking, but SEC staff statements, exemptive orders or items on the Unified Agenda were not checked. The SEC's digital asset actions (Mandate p. 835) are not covered here. Progress is a judgment call: proposals are not final, and only the CAT exemption and cost amendment are operative. A Federal Register query for SEC final rules published since 2026-06-01, run 2026-10-17, returned eight technical or administrative items (EDGAR Filer Manual, quorum requirement, Form PF compliance date, governance technical amendments, delegations, FDTA data standards, Form X-17A-5, a correction) and no final offering, reporting or filer-status rule. The CAT concept release (Release No. 34-105251) seeks comment on basic aspects of the CAT, including what the release calls its existential aspects, but proposes no rule; its 2026-04-20 Federal Register date was not verified in this review. The 2026-09-30 accredited investor items are requests for comment whose comment periods run from a later Federal Register publication.
